factors.name: aapl_vol10_to_vol20_x_qqq_trend
factors.hypothesis: Vol-ratio direction depends on the market regime; rising Apple vol in an uptrending QQQ differs from a downtrend, so signing by QQQ trend lets linear models use it.

factors.name: msft_ret_rank_vs_own_range
factors.hypothesis: MSFT 1d return was useful; scaling by MSFT's same-day range (rather than a slow 60d std) captures how decisive the move was within the day with less lag.

factors.name: aapl_downside_vol_10d
factors.hypothesis: Downside-only volatility measures fear separately from total volatility, which was the most important feature, and may hint at mean reversion after selloffs.

factors.name: aapl_gap_fill_pressure
factors.formula: multiply(safe_divide(subtract(AAPL_Open, lag(AAPL_Close, 1)), lag(AAPL_Close, 1)), safe_divide(subtract(AAPL_Close, AAPL_Open), AAPL_Open))
factors.hypothesis: Product of overnight gap and intraday return is negative when the day faded the gap; fades may predict continuation or reversal next day.

factors.name: qqq_ret_zscore_20d_regime
factors.hypothesis: Apple volatility is key; a standardised QQQ shock tells the model whether the market is making abnormal moves, complementing Apple's own vol level.

factors.name: aapl_ret_vs_qqq_vol_scaled
factors.hypothesis: Apple's excess move over QQQ scaled by market vol complements the MSFT lead signal, indicating whether Apple lagged or overshot sector direction.
